title: What happens when two packages contain the same class name
answer: Java allows different packages to declare classes with the same simple name because their fully qualified names are different. A caller can import one simple name and refer to the other with its fully qualified name, or use fully qualified names for both. Importing two types with the same simple name into one compilation unit creates ambiguity, so the code must disambiguate. Packages therefore provide a namespace rather than requiring every class in an application to have a globally unique simple name.
